ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Business Corporations Act (Ontario) (OBCA), R.S.O. 1990, c. B.16, ss. 21.1-21.2 (Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register), and O. Reg. 62/13; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), S.C. 2001, c. 41, as amended (FINTRAC reporting and record-keeping regime); Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, Part XII.2 (money-laundering offences); Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), S.C. 2017, c. 21; FINTRAC Policy Interpretation and Guidance on Politically Exposed Persons (updated 2023); federal beneficial-ownership reform (Bill C-42, royal assent June 2024) amends the Canada Business Corporations Act in stages to permit limited public access to beneficial ownership data once fully in force.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of the foreign director's or UBO's country, certified and notarized by a local notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for Apostille Convention states, including Canada from 11 January 2024); Consular Legalization through the Embassy or High Commission of Canada for non-Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each director and UBO (utility bill or bank account statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank in the country of residence, notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization by a competent authority in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and Certificate of Good Standing for any corporate shareholder or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent or corporate registry in the parent entity's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization through the parent jurisdiction's designated competent authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration and statutory declaration identifying the individuals with significant control and the source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction, or a Commissioner for Taking Affidavits in Ontario if signed domestically
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign notarized declarations; domestic sworn declaration executed before an Ontario commissioner without apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders and UBOs against FINTRAC's domestic and foreign PEP categories, including family members and close associates, per the PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance; mandatory verification against Global Affairs Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, designations under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Sergei Magnitsky Law, and United Nations Security Council consolidated lists; market-standard cross-check of the OFAC SDN List and US sanctions for cross-border transactions routed through SWIFT; adverse-media investigation and corporate ownership-lineage check required for every entity in the ownership chain. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for the Medium_Risk_Enhanced classification of a passive equity-holding SPV, including source-of-wealth documentation, independent director identity verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ontario Business Registry (operated by the Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, incorporating the Companies Office of Ontario), accessible at www.ontario.ca/page/ontario-business-registry; NUANS preliminary name search report obtained through accredited NUANS search houses.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under OBCA s. 9 and O. Reg. 62/13, corporate names may be in English, French, or bilingual form; characters must be drawn from the standard English and French alphabets, with accents permitted; the name must be distinguishable from existing Ontario, federal, and registered extra-provincial corporate names and from reserved names; a numbered company designation, e.g., 1234567 Ontario Inc., is exempt from name clearance and remains available for the SPV; proper legal ending is mandatory, e.g., Inc., Corp., Limited, Ltd., or the French equivalents.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name may be re-submitted with a revised NUANS report. If the rejection is grounded in distinguishability or a prohibited or sensitive token, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the Director under OBCA s. 10(4) within 30 days of the refusal notice, stating the grounds on which the proposed name is registrable. If the Director upholds the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Ontario Superior Court of Justice by way of judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. J.1, and the Administrative Tribunals Support Act. Director-level review takes approximately 5-10 business days; the practical alternative remedy is to select a new name and file a fresh NUANS search or proceed with a numbered company. Extension of the 90-day reservation window requires filing of a new NUANS search and payment of the applicable search fee before expiry of the current reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual or mail-forwarding address is not acceptable as a registered office. OBCA s. 14(1) requires every Ontario corporation to maintain a registered office at a physical street address in Ontario capable of accepting service of process, and corporate records must be accessible at that location. For a passive equity-holding SPV, a commercial registered-office service is permissible provided it supplies a physical Ontario street address and an on-site facility that handles statutory documents and service of process; the address must be stated in the articles and annual return, and any change must be filed under s. 14(2). Industry classification is medium-risk holdco, and banking AML/KYC policies generally reject mailbox-only addresses; a physical registered-agent office in an Ontario business district is the standard compliant arrangement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% aggregate annual probability of a compliance visit or audit inspection: approximately 8% probability of a CRA corporate tax or GST/HST compliance audit, including address-verification correspondence, in any year; approximately 5% probability of a physical registered-office verification by the Ontario Business Registry or a service-of-process attempt; less than 2% probability of an unannounced AML site visit because a pure holding SPV is not itself an FINTRAC reporting entity; on-site inspection risk materially increases only if the SPV later engages in lending, treasury, or securities activities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Ontario), R.S.O. 1990, c. B.10, as amended (OBCA), including sections 4 (incorporation), 5 (articles), 8 (registered office), 14 (directors), 49 (share subscriptions), and 106 (first directors); companion regulation O. Reg. 62/06 under the Ontario Business Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery (MPBSD), Ontario Business Registry; Corporations and Registries Division.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (OBCA Form 1) filed electronically through the Ontario Business Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital prescribed for OBCA corporations; the subscribed share capital is established in the articles of incorporation and may be issued for any lawful consideration. No escrow or capital deposit is mandated by statute.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation's Articles of Incorporation be and are hereby confirmed and adopted; that the share subscription of the subscribers as set forth in the initial share subscription register be and is hereby accepted and the corresponding shares be issued upon receipt of lawful consideration; that the registered office address shown in the articles be and is hereby confirmed as the Corporation's registered office in Ontario; that the individuals named as first directors be and are hereby appointed to hold office until their successors are elected; and that the officers named in the officer register be and are hereby appointed with usual authority, and management is authorized to complete filings and open banking accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry online portal; Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name search through the NUANS database and obtain a Nuans search report. For an Ontario business corporation, file a name reservation request if desired (optional). In case the proposed name contains a special element or closely resembles an existing trademark, obtain a consent letter from the right holder.
required_dossiers: Consent letter for distinctive name elements (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name search report is queried or a name is refused, file a revised name submission or request a Name Reservation Review through the Ontario Business Registry within 15 days; supply rebuttal evidence of distinguishability.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Executing Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry online incorporation service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete OBCA Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation) setting out the corporate name, class and maximum number of shares, restrictions on share transfer, number of directors, first directors, registered office address, and any permitted restrictions on business. Articles must be executed by a subscriber director or authorized representative and submitted electronically together with the required declaration and fee.
required_dossiers: NUANS search report and name reservation (if used)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Articles are rejected for statutory non-compliance or insufficient particulars, amend and resubmit via the Ontario Business Registry; an incorporated corporation can subsequently file Articles of Amendment (OBCA Form 3) to cure permitted defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry (online portal administered by MPBSD).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles of Incorporation and the completed authorization for initial registered office and first directors through the Ontario Business Registry. Pay the electronic filing fee by credit card or authorized account; upon approval the registry issues a Certificate of Incorporation evidenced by an Ontario Business Registry extract.
required_dossiers: Initial registered office and first directors authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If filing is placed under review, promptly respond to requests for clarification; if missing information is identified, resubmit with corrected data. Registry rulings may be appealed administratively to MPBSD within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation itself; directors and shareholders acting under OBCA sections 1(1), 14, 107 and Regulations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting (or adopt written resolutions) to confirm directors and officers, adopt bylaws, approve the issuance of shares reflected in the initial share subscription, establish corporate records within Ontario (including minute book, share register, and securities register), and appoint an authorized signatory for the bank and registry. Complete Ontario Record of Registered Office and Directors (OBCA Form 2) if any change occurs, and file any subsequent notice as required.
required_dossiers: Minutes of first board meeting or written consent resolutions
Share subscription register and share certificates
Officer appointment records and acknowledgment forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If omission in organizational documents is discovered, ratify by subsequent board or shareholder resolution; if a formal registry filing of officer or director changes is required, submit OBCA Form 2 or Form 6 via the Ontario Business Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office, Extraprovincial Considerations, and Post-Incorporation Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry, Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), and applicable municipal offices.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure registered office address is within Ontario and effective service of process is accepted. If the corporation is eligible for the Canada Business Corporations Act and conducts extraprovincial activity, consider an extra-provincial registration in other Canadian provinces. Open corporate bank account using the certificate and omnibus corporate records; apply for any CRA business number, and complete obligatory corporate information returns within statutory periods.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Ontario Business Registry extract
Corporate minute book and share register
Any required extra-provincial registration form for other provinces
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or registry notices are received for late or incorrect filings, file the required initial return or amendment electronically; any registration deficiency can be cured by filing the requisite late form with supporting explanations under applicable compliance provisions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: N/A – Pure equity holding SPV holds no operational facility and requires no industrial operating permission under Ontario or federal industry licensing statutes.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for passive holding company; no commercial unit, manufacturing plant, or public-facing operation is established.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment, Conservation and Parks, Ontario (MECP); federal component may be administered by Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) if a physical footprint exists.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no physical premises, no discharges, no land disturbance; no Environmental Assessment Act registration or approval applicable to a passive equity holding company.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; the SPV intentionally avoids operations that generate wastewater, volatile organic compounds, or hazardous waste. If future operating subsidiaries emit Regulated Substances, MECP regulations (O. Reg. 419/05 for air emissions and O. Reg. 259/05 for waste) will apply at the subsidiary level.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable – the corporation maintains no employees, leased premises, or physical infrastructure; therefore fire safety certification, structural load inspections, and workplace safety clearance (Occupational Health and Safety Act) are not triggered. The registered office is limited to a mailing location under OBCA.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) is the single federal tax authority for corporate income tax, GST/HST, and payroll; self-service portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-businesses/business-account.html) and Business Registration Online (BRO). Ontario Ministry of Finance and the Ontario Business Registry (https://www.ontario.ca/page/ontario-business-registry) are the provincial counterpart for Ontario incorporation records, Ontario corporate tax (administered federally by the CRA under a single-administration tax collection agreement), and Employer Health Tax (EHT). Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) governs customs/export reporting infrastructure (Canadian Export Reporting System, CERS) relevant to export substantiation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Procedure for a foreign-owned Business Corporation (federal or Ontario) to obtain its statutory tax identity: (1) Incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act or Ontario Business Corporations Act; obtain the Ontario/federal corporate registration number from the Ontario Business Registry or Corporations Canada. (2) Register with the CRA through Business Registration Online (BRO) to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN), the universal tax identifier under which the CRA assigns account-type suffixes: corporate income tax account (RP0001) is mandatory for every resident corporation; GST/HST account (RT0001) is obligatory only if taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold, otherwise voluntary; payroll account (RP0001) is required if the SPV compensates directors/employees; import/export account (RM0001) is required if the SPV imports or exports commercial goods. (3) For a non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada or earning Canadian-source income, register via Form RC113 (being a non-resident) and obtain a CRA non-resident account; consider a Section 116 income tax clearance certificate for future dispositions of taxable Canadian property. (4) For Ontario, the CRA collects Ontario corporate income tax through the combined federal-provincial registration; separately register for EHT with the Ontario Ministry of Finance only if the SPV has payroll in Ontario. (5) A pure equity holding SPV with only passive dividend inflows and no taxable supplies has minimal registration obligations: the mandatory account is the corporate income tax account; GST/HST registration is optional and typically inadvisable as it restricts input tax credit recovery on exempt financial services; no provincial sales tax registration applies in Ontario because HST is fully federally administered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope – A Canadian-incorporated Business Corporation is a separate legal taxpayer subject to federal Part I income tax and Ontario corporate income tax at the entity level on its worldwide income if resident in Canada (taxation on worldwide income with foreign tax credits under section 126); a non-resident corporation is taxable only on Canadian-source income (section 115) and may elect to file on a Canadian branch basis. No pass-through or check-the-box election exists in Canadian law; the pure equity holding SPV is a taxable entity whose dividends received from taxable Canadian corporations are fully deductible under the intercorporate dividend deduction (section 112) and dividends from foreign affiliates may be deductible under section 113 (exempt-surplus basket), making the HoldCo a conduit for tax-effective dividend repatriation. Canada applies no tax-exempt zones; the SPV cannot be a tax-exempt entity except as a non-profit or government-owned corporation, which is not available for a commercial holding structure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not recognize U.S.-style check-the-box entity classification; classification is determined by corporate law and tax treaty residence. Statutory elections available to an equity-holding SPV include: (1) section 85 rollover election to transfer property (including shares) into the corporation on a tax-deferred basis at elected amounts between cost and fair market value; (2) section 88(2) plan-of-arrangement or wind-up rollover election for subsidiary amalgamation/wind-up; (3) section 93 foreign affiliate election to deem additional dividends on a disposition of foreign affiliate shares, converting capital gains into deductible dividends; (4) section 83(2) capital dividend account election to distribute tax-free capital dividends (relevant if the SPV receives life insurance proceeds or capital gains eligible to the capital dividend account); (5) section 114/115 election regimes for non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada; (6) voluntary GST/HST registration election. Hybrid mismatch: Canada enacted BEPS Action 2 hybrid mismatch denial rules effective for payments made after July 1, 2022 (Income Tax Act sections 18.4 and 18.5), disallowing deductions on hybrid instruments, hybrid transfers, deductible hybrid distributions and dual-inclusion outcomes; a master holding SPV should documentation-test intra-group financing, preferred share structures and back-to-back arrangements to avoid result-8 deduction disallowances and to preserve the intercorporate dividend deduction integrity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) – Canada's federal value-added tax administered by the CRA under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; Ontario joined the harmonized system effective July 1, 2010, applying a single HST rate comprising the 5% federal GST component and the 8% Ontario provincial component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Small-supplier threshold: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies (excluding exempt supplies, incidental supplies and certain financial services) per calendar quarter and cumulatively over the preceding four calendar quarters triggers mandatory registration. A pure equity holding SPV receives dividends and capital gains, which are not consideration for a supply (exempt financial services or non-supplies), so no compulsory GST/HST registration arises unless the SPV makes taxable supplies exceeding CAD 30,000 (e.g., management fees, administrative recharge services to subsidiaries, interest on intercompany loan facilities if not an exempt financial service). Non-resident suppliers of specified digital services and short-term accommodation have no registration threshold under the simplified non-resident GST/HST regime, which is not typical for an equity holding SPV but is noted for completeness.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose a mandatory real-time electronic fiscal clearance, digital stamping, invoice pre-authorization, or government-side e-invoicing approval system comparable to Latin American or southern European regimes. The CRA permits electronic invoices in any reliable format provided the registrant retains records satisfying Excise Tax Act section 286 (auditability, retrievability, six-year retention). The CRA supports voluntary business-to-government e-invoicing through the Pan-Canadian Trust Framework and publishes PEPPOL PINT/UBL technical specifications for B2B interoperability. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically through GST/HST NETFILE or approved third-party EDI/API software; CRA My Business Account is the transactional portal for assessments, adjustments and instalments. Ontario has no separate provincial e-invoice clearance mechanism because HST is federally collected. Selected listed financial institutions (SLFIs) – relevant only if the SPV is, or holds 10% or more of, a bank, trust, insurer or other listed financial institution under the SLFI attribution regime effective July 1, 2021 (and the December 2023/2024 draft expansion of the financial-institution definition to certain significantly-holding corporations) – must file annual GST/HST returns computing interprovincial HST attribution using the special attribution method (SAM) formula, file by the SLFI due dates, and maintain attribution data in electronic format; a non-financial pure equity HoldCo is outside this regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A registered pure equity holding SPV may claim 0% GST/HST on: (a) goods exported from Canada by the supplier, provided the goods are removed from Canada as soon as is reasonable (normally within 60 days) after the sale, are not further processed in Canada, and the supplier retains documentary proof of export under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act; (b) services supplied to a non-resident person that are not rendered in respect of real or tangible personal property situated in Canada and not for consumption/use in Canada (Schedule VI, Part V, section 7), e.g., group management and administrative services recharged to foreign subsidiaries; (c) financial services are NOT zero-rated – dividends, interest and capital gains from shareholding are exempt supplies or non-supplies and never invoke the zero-rating mechanism toward input tax credit recovery. The zero-rating eligibility is conditioned on the registrant having a GST/HST account, issuing a zero-rated invoice with the BN/RT prefix, receiving consideration, and maintaining contemporaneous export documentation. Pure passive dividend receipt cannot itself produce an input tax credit or refund.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Commercial Export Declaration (Form B13A or e-customs B13A) transmitted through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), including 10-digit HS tariff classification, customs entry number, export/import client identifier and original receipt indicator

Bill of Lading / air waybill / truck carrier manifest / courier waybill evidencing physical movement of goods from Canada to a foreign destination, with shipper, consignee, port of exit, and dated carrier signature
Sales contract and commercial invoice bearing the zero-rating reference (Excise Tax Act Schedule VI, Part V) and the SPV's GST/HST registration number
Inward Remittance Certificate, foreign exchange brokerage confirmation, or bank transfer advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds in the invoiced currency and amount
ETA section 286 records: purchase orders, insurance certificates, customs correspondence, packing lists, and foreign non-resident status evidence (if claiming zero-rated services)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess GST/HST returns within four years (extended to seven years for misrepresentation or neglect; unlimited in fraud cases) and claw back zero-rating benefits and input tax credits where export documentation is incomplete or inconsistent. Penalties under Excise Tax Act subsection 285(1) for false statements or omissions: CAD 250 plus 25% of the net tax understated or refund overstated where the person acted knowingly or under circumstances amounting to gross negligence; concurrent Income Tax Act subsection 163(2) gross-negligence penalties of 50% of understated tax may apply on related adjustments to intercompany income. Willful evasion is a criminal offense under ETA section 327 punishable on summary conviction by a fine of not less than 50% and not more than 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and/or up to two years' imprisonment, and on indictment by a fine of 50%–200% of the tax sought to be evaded and/or up to five years' imprisonment. Arrears interest compounds daily at the CRA prescribed rate plus any applicable provincial-FRIL component; retroactive clawbacks may also trigger Part IV tax reassessment and transfer-pricing audits under ITA section 247(2) if export proceeds are not repatriated within commercially reasonable terms (CRA generally applies a 180-day benchmark for related-party export payment cycles, with documented extension only where transfer-pricing terms are arm's length). CRA/CBSA may conduct verifications through the post-audit verification program, demand proof of physical export, and issue Form GST/RC 163 letters; failure to substantiate results in reversal to 13% HST (Ontario) or 5% GST plus interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); no separate foreign-exchange administration exists. The Foreign Exchange Control Act was suspended in 1951 and repealed in 1992. Functional oversight is split: OSFI supervises banks offering FX products, FINTRAC enforces AML/EFT reporting, and the Department of Finance Canada administers economic sanctions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for current and capital account items. No exchange-control approvals are required for inward equity, intra-group loans, dividend repatriation, or liquidation proceeds. Profit remittance hurdles are fiscal and corporate only: (1) OBCA s. 130 solvency test for dividend declarations; (2) Part XIII withholding under the Income Tax Act (25% statutory, treaty-reduced, e.g., Canada-US treaty permits 5% for a non-resident parent owning at least 10% of voting shares); (3) sanctions screening under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation window for export receipts. A pure equity holding SPV has no export proceeds; residual compliance consists of FINTRAC EFT reporting for wire transfers of CAD 10,000 or more and Statistics Canada balance-of-payments surveys for non-resident direct investment.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. FINTRAC-registered corporate EMIs are lawful money-service businesses under the PCMLTFA but cannot take redeemable deposits or conduct 'banking business' without a Schedule I bank licence under the Bank Act (s. 541). They are viable as secondary pre-funding corridors for small recurring disbursements but unacceptable as the sole capital-escrow rail due to absence of CDIC deposit insurance, higher counterparty event risk, and narrower acceptance of source-of-wealth documentation for a passive holdco.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Not a statutory mandate, but standard Schedule I bank policy requires identity verification of all directors and authorized signatories. A new-to-bank Ontario corporation is generally required to have at least one signing director or authorized signatory attend an in-branch interview in Canada. Remote opening is available on exception when a video-call interview is combined with notarized government-issued ID, certified true copies of corporate records, and a completed non-attestation questionnaire; fully frictionless remote opening without an interview is rarely accepted for non-resident-controlled Ontario holdcos.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Single-purpose, zero-employee holdco receiving a large equity injection within 90 days of account opening; low-substance red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ontario Corporate Profile Report issued within 30 days; certificate of incorporation and final articles; share register; executed capital-subscription agreement; audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements of the parent; 90-day source-of-funds bank statements from the contributing parent; organizational chart extending to ultimate individual owners; statutory declaration; business-purpose memorandum citing ISIC 6420 and the specific subsidiaries to be held; board resolution authorizing account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident parent funding from a jurisdiction with weak AML enforcement or through layered intermediary or trust structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial-ownership attestation through every layer; intermediary bank statements tracing the specific funds; trust deed or settlement deed and trustee resolution where a trust is in the chain; PEP and sanctions-clearance screens for every UBO and director; explanation letter for the use of intermediaries; certified copies of identity documents for all 25%-or-greater UBOs; the OBCA register of individuals with significant control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Funnel risk: holdco passes subscriber funds downstream to a subsidiary or pays dividends to the non-resident parent shortly after funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fund-flow model and settlement calendar; executed investment or subscription agreements with target subsidiaries; board minutes authorizing each downstream capital call and each dividend; OBCA s. 130 solvency certificate signed at each declaration; NR4 and Part XIII withholding remittance plan; parent tax-residency certificates for treaty-reduced withholding (Canada-US Form NR301); bank letter confirming the segregated Capital Escrow Account designation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder loans or intercompany promissory notes alongside equity, triggering thin-capitalization scrutiny and suspicion of disguised treasury banking.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed shareholder loan agreements with arm's-length interest rates; intercompany promissory notes; CRA Form T106 where reportable; transfer-pricing documentation under ITA s. 247; debt-capacity analysis and book-value-of-assets calculation supporting the OBCA solvency test; board-approved group treasury policy restricting lending activity; CRS and CbCR ownership declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Contingent-liability mismatch: holdco requested to issue guarantees, letters of comfort, or backstops for lenders of portfolio companies, contradicting the 'pure equity holding' sub-type.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group guarantee policy; Ontario legal opinion on guarantee and indemnity validity; consolidated financial statements proving substantive capitalization; board resolutions specifically authorizing each guarantee; asset charge and collateral certification; disclosure to bank compliance confirming the contingent liability is passive and not deposit-taking; applicable securities exemptions under NI 45-106 if guaranteed debt securities are issued.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: No Canadian regulatory approval or purpose-code license is required. Route the injection by SWIFT gpi MT103 from the parent's bank into the Ontario holdco's Tier-1 account. For USD funding, settle intraday over Fedwire through the Canadian bank's U.S. correspondent; for CAD funding, use Payments Canada Lynx (successor to LVTS). MT103 fields: 50K (non-resident parent account), 59 (Ontario holdco with full address), 70 (Remittance Information: 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION // CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION // ISIC 6420 HOLDCO // SUB-FUND-REF'), 72 (Sender to Correspondent: 'OP-ACCT XXXX'). Nature of payment: 'Capital contribution (non-repayable)'. Banks internally map the flow to balance-of-payments direct-investment classifications and report to FINTRAC if at least CAD 10,000. Pre-notify the relationship manager 48 hours in advance with the funding resolution and source-of-funds trace pack.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail is SWIFT gpi MT103 for all cross-border capital calls, acquisition consummations, and dividend remittances. For CAD domestic high-value payments use Payments Canada Lynx rather than batch EFT; for recurring USD operating payments use U.S. ACH or Fedwire through the Canadian bank's correspondent network. Settlement proof consists of MT103 confirmation, SWIFT gpi tracker output, and bank-issued monthly statements. Documentary commercial LCs are unnecessary for a pure equity holdco but should be established through the Tier-1 trade desk if the SPV is later required to issue performance guarantees or standby LCs on behalf of portfolio companies; such facilities must be UCP 600-compliant, governed by ISBP 745, and approved by the bank's credit committee as contingent liabilities.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forwards (CAD/USD) transacted under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and CSA, or a bank-only FX Master Agreement, settled payment-versus-payment through CLS where available.
FX swaps covering principal and interest exchanges for temporary inter-subsidiary funding sweeps with maturities up to 12 months.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps converting USD-denominated intercompany debt into CAD obligations, subject to OBCA solvency certification and board derivative-authority resolution.
Exchange-traded FX futures and vanilla FX options on the Montreal Exchange (TMX), qualifying for exemption from OSFI B-7 uncleared-margin requirements.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) are legally permissible but commercially disfavored for CAD because the Canadian dollar is fully deliverable; NDFs are used only where the counterparty jurisdiction restricts outright conversion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Annual Return (OBCA s. 262) — corporate information and director/officer update filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery — ServiceOntario Corporate Registry (Director under the OBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary date of incorporation (e.g., anniversary May 15 → due July 14)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Two consecutive years of non-filing permits the Director to administratively dissolve/strike off the corporation after notice (OBCA s. 240/241); each director or officer in default is liable to a fine of up to CAD 2,000; reinstatement after strike-off requires court and government fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return — combined federal and Ontario corporate income tax return (includes supporting schedules for dividend income and capital gains)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the taxation year-end (e.g., a December 31 year-end → due by June 30 of the following calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delay (maximum 12 months); repeat failures attract 10% plus 2% per month; statutory daily fines of CAD 25/day up to CAD 2,500 (CAD 100/day up to CAD 25,000 for large corporations under ITA s. 162); arrears interest accrues at the CRA prescribed rate plus 2% for corporations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: OBCA Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) annual confirmation — beneficial ownership register filing for the pure equity holding SPV
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery — ServiceOntario ISC filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, filed together with the OBCA Annual Return within 60 days after the incorporation anniversary; interim updates must be filed within 15 days of any share transfer or change in significant control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: OBCA offence provisions: individuals (directors/officers) liable to fines up to CAD 100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 6 months; corporations liable to fines up to CAD 500,000; sustained non-compliance may trigger administrative strike-off and adverse bank/KYC reassessment of the SPV.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based statutory audit threshold under the OBCA; a private corporation is exempt from appointing an auditor where it has fewer than 15 shareholders and all shareholders consent, or obtains unanimous shareholder agreement to dispense with the audit (standard for a single-shareholder HoldCo). Audited financial statements are mandatory for public issuers and corporations offering securities to the public.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: CPA Canada Handbook — IFRS (mandatory for public/listed enterprises) or ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises), both accepted as Canadian GAAP by the CRA; the pure equity holding SPV may apply ASPE.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the OBCA ISC regime (in force January 1, 2023), the corporation must maintain a current register of individuals with significant control (≥25% of voting rights, fair market value of shares, or de facto control) and file ISC information annually with ServiceOntario as part of the OBCA Annual Return; each annual filing confirms unchanged ownership or incorporates changes, with interim updates due within 15 days of any share transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholder ledger with full transfer history)
Register of Directors (and Officers, if any)
Minute Book (articles, certificates, annual resolutions, meeting minutes)
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 400 – CAD 1,200 (≈ USD 290 – 880) per year for a commercial registered office address and corporate agent in Ontario, inclusive of mail forwarding and annual return filing support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 6,000 – CAD 15,000 (≈ USD 4,400 – 11,000) for a full audit of a simple HoldCo; CAD 1,500 – CAD 4,000 (≈ USD 1,100 – 2,900) for a CPA review or compilation when the audit is validly waived

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% (federal 15.0% + Ontario general corporate tax 11.5%; passive investment income of a non-small-business corporation is subject to the same general corporate rates, with no Ontario small business deduction applicable to a pure equity holding SPV)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Subsection 112(1) intercorporate dividend deduction effectively eliminates Part I tax on taxable dividends received from a 'taxable Canadian corporation' held as a portfolio asset or from an operating subsidiary; Part IV refundable tax on look-through dividends is recovered via the RDTOH mechanism when dividends are later distributed to non-resident shareholders; no direct provincial tax holiday applies to pure equity holding vehicles; the Ontario Innovation Tax Credit and other provincial credits are generally unavailable to passive holdcos.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (T2) filed electronically through CRA-certified tax preparation software or CRA 'My Business Account' portal; T2 NETFILE service provider e-filing is mandatory for most corporations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, based on the corporation's fiscal taxation year; instalment payments of estimated tax are required quarterly where the corporation's taxable income and province tax exceed statutory thresholds.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return must be filed on or before the last day of the sixth month following the end of the taxation year (e.g., a December 31 fiscal year-end requires filing no later than June 30 of the following calendar year); balance-due instalment dates are 2-month/3-month staggered instalments for small and large corporations respectively.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name, 15-digit Business Number, jurisdiction of registration, registered Canadian head office address, mailing address, fiscal period start and end dates, corporation type, and Canadian activity code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation that is required to file a T2 must provide a Canadian head-office address, an authorized Canadian representative, and the non-resident treaty jurisdiction address; the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) may require the completion of Form RC4178 to support the deemed-residential or non-resident tax treaty position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate of gross revenue and all income amounts: dividends received, interest, capital gains, royalties and rental revenue computed under Part I of the Income Tax Act (Canada).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident holdcos must attribute only Canadian-source income amounts; foreign-source dividends and capital gains are reported on the T2 as required but may be taxable unless exempt under section 113 or treaty-protected under an applicable income tax convention.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims the deduction available under subsection 112(1) of the Income Tax Act for taxable dividends received from taxable Canadian corporations; the amount is included in total income and then deducted, reducing net taxable income to nil for pure intercorporate dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-controlled corporations may deduct fully only if the dividend payer is a taxable Canadian corporation and the recipient corporation is a Canadian-resident taxpayer; dividends received from a direct foreign subsidiary generally qualify for the section 113 foreign affiliate dividend deduction only with respect to the affiliate's surplus account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of net income after all deductions, non-capital loss carryforwards, capital loss carryforwards, and special allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Taxable income for a non-resident corporation is limited to income attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment plus Canadian-source net capital gains; losses can be deducted only to the extent permitted under Part I and the relevant tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 160 / federal schedule (Part I tax payable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax calculated at 15% on taxable income less applicable tax credits, foreign tax credits, and federal investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents entitled to treaty benefits complete a treaty disclosure form and provide a Certificate of Residency (TRC) to substantiate reduced federal tax rates where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Ontario T2 provincial page / Line 390 (Ontario corporate tax payable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ontario provincial tax at 11.5% general rate computed on Ontario allocated taxable income; if the holding corporation has no permanent establishment in Ontario, the province will not levy provincial tax on the income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident corporations deemed to have a permanent establishment in Ontario, the provincial tax is calculated under the Ontario Corporations Tax Act based on the establishment's reported income and expenses; otherwise the federal T2 directs provincial tax to the province of permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 7 (Capital gains/portfolio dividends and aggregate investment income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies Canadian-source dividends and taxable capital gains from dispositions of shares; required for calculating the refundable Part I tax on aggregate investment income for private corporations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-controlled private corporations will compute Part IV dividend refund tax on portfolio dividends; treaty exemptions may not apply to the Canadian-source portion where the non-resident's treaty home does not waive source tax on dividends from portfolio shareholdings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months (maximum 17% of the unsettled federal tax); additional 10% penalty for repeat failures within a three-year period; daily penalty for failing to file an information slip (e.g., T106) is $24 per day, minimum $100 and maximum $12,500 for each information return; false-tax-evasion penalty under subsection 163.2 is the greater of $24,000 and 50% of the understated tax; CRA may assess interest on unremitted balance-due amounts at the prescribed rate, compounding daily.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada), imposed on dividends paid or credited by the Canadian corporation to a non-resident shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced withholding rate under an income tax treaty, the non-resident beneficial owner must: (1) obtain an official Certificate of Residency (TRC) from its local tax authority for each calendar year; (2) provide the TRC and its legal name, address, and treaty residence address to the Canadian paying corporation; (3) file Form NR301 (Application for a Reduction in the Amount of Non-Resident Tax Withheld) with the CRA or instruct the paying corporation to withhold at the treaty rate based on the submitted certificates; (4) where required, submit Form NR302 when the treaty claim is based on a partnership or hybrid entity; and (5) annex appropriate treaty-comfort letters and the corporate ownership chain evidencing the beneficial owner's real and not conduit status. The Canadian payer must retain all documentation and may require an amended T2 or NR return where the reduction was improperly applied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates under Part XIII: interest 25%, royalties 25% (with limited exemptions for certain copyrights and software under the Income Tax Act). Treaty rates are DTA-dependent; under the Canada-US tax treaty, arm's-length interest may be sourced at a nil or 15% rate depending on the payer affiliation, while royalty withholding is reduced to 10% for most IP classes; other treaties commonly provide 10% royalty and 10–15% interest ceilings where the shareholder owns 10% or more of the voting stock and the recipient is the beneficial owner.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: There is no formal CAD-denominated Local File/Master File threshold in Canadian domestic law; however, section 247 of the Income Tax Act and the CRA's Information Circular IC87-2R require contemporaneous documentation for all non-arm's-length transactions with related non-residents where the aggregate fair market value of the reportable transactions exceeds CAD 1,000,000 for a single related party in a fiscal year; additionally, Form T106 must be filed where the aggregate value of all specified transactions with all non-arm's-length non-residents surpasses CAD 1,000,000 annually, and the larger of the CRA 'reasonable efforts' standard requires documentation irrespective of size where the taxpayer claims transfer-pricing relief.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has not adopted a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime equivalent to the UAE or offshore financial centres. Instead, a pure equity holding SPV claiming treaty or domestic law advantages is assessed under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (section 245 of the Income Tax Act), the 'substance versus form' doctrine, and CRA's administrative practice under the OECD Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) Action 6. Indicators of unacceptable economic substance include: absence of Canadian resident directors, meetings held entirely outside Canada, management functions exercised abroad, lack of local bank accounts or accounting records, conduits used to round-trip funds to an offshore parent, and no commercial rationale other than the realization of a tax benefit. A transaction found to be an 'avoidance transaction' can trigger full reassessment and a 50% penalty on the net tax benefit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully filing a false or incomplete T2 return, omitting reportable dividend income, fabricating deductible interest or management fees, disguising a taxable disposition of shares as a tax-free return of capital, or providing false documentation to the CRA to obtain treaty withholding reductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under subsection 163(2) of the Income Tax Act, a 50% civil penalty of the tax attempted to be evaded; under section 239 of the Income Tax Act, a conviction for tax evasion is punishable by a fine of not more than 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to five years; restitution and court-ordered forfeiture of the proceeds of crime available to the Crown.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who authorize or participate in tax evasion may be personally assessed for the corporate tax shortfall under the criminal restitution doctrine, face disqualification from acting as directors under the Canada Business Corporations Act, and may be subject to extradition and travel bans where the evasion involves treaty fraud, tax flight, or money laundering; subsection 227.1 of the Income Tax Act makes directors personally liable for unremitted employee source deductions and GST/HST.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a pure equity holding SPV in Canada without actual management, directors, employees, bank accounts, or independent economic activities, where the sole purpose is to access a treaty rate or defer Canada's Part I tax on dividends that were intended to flow directly to an ultimate non-resident parent; knowingly presenting the SPV as a resident company while all decisions are taken in a lower-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may apply the GAAR under subsection 245(2), deeming the SPV's separate legal personality ineffective; tax benefit is denied, and a 50% penalty may be assessed on the benefit at the time of the assessment; CRA may also impose transfer-pricing reassessment and withhold the non-resident's income under the treaty abuse provisions (e.g., section 145.1 of the Income Tax Act for hybrid mismatch arrangements).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell entity may be jointly and severally liable for the corporation's unpaid withholding tax if they knowingly signed remittance returns or directed the diversion of funds; the CRA has authority to issue 'section 160' transfers where assets were distributed to a non-arm's-length individual or corporate shareholder without adequate consideration, making the recipient personally liable for the tax balance; criminal courts may impose director travel bans and personal bankruptcy where the evasion exceeds CAD 10 million.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the holding SPV as a financial channel without registering as a Money Services Business (MSB) or reporting suspicious transactions under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); failing to maintain a Canadian registered record of ultimate beneficial owners; accepting loans or dividend distributions from an unidentified source; conducting cross-border wire transfers that exceed CAD 10,000 without FINTRAC reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties assessed by FINTRAC of up to CAD 500,000 for violations (and up to CAD 2,000,000 for repeat offenders); the Payment Card Network (PCN) guidelines do not exempt medium-risk holdco structures; failure to file a Suspicious Transaction Report or Electronic Funds Transfer Report may trigger a separate conviction with a fine of up to CAD 500,000 and imprisonment for up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers can receive personal penalties for AML non-compliance where they deliberately or recklessly omit record-keeping and reporting obligations; under PCMLTFA section 75.1, personal liability reaches CAD 100,000 per individual; where the company is used to commit fraud or criminal financing, the individual can be prosecuted as a principal and, if convicted, prohibited from re-entering Canada and subject to search-and-seizure of personal assets under a restraining order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Information Return Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into non-arm's-length cross-border financing, guarantee, management service, or IP royalty arrangements involving the holdco without charging arm's-length consideration; failing to file Form T106 for reportable transactions within six months of the taxation year-end; failing to maintain contemporaneous documentation that demonstrates a reasonable effort to satisfy the arm's-length principle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of net income to arm's-length amount plus a transfer-pricing penalty of 10% of the net adjustment (minimum CAD 1,000, maximum CAD 100,000 amount per assessment? actually 10% statutory minimum applies), plus interest; where the taxpayer fails to file T106, the daily penalty is CAD 24 per day up to CAD 12,500; if the pricing is considered gross negligence or willful misrepresentation, the 50% civil penalty under s.163.2 may be assessed instead.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who attest to the accuracy of T106 filings or sign T2 returns can be held liable for the civil penalty where they intentionally misrepresent the arm's-length nature of the transactions; transfer-pricing penalties are normally assessed against the corporation, but under the 'ordinary business care' doctrine, directors who knew or should have known of the false pricing may be jointly liable for the unremitted tax, and CRA may seek an order prohibiting international travel and requiring the posting of security for unpaid assessments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Maintain Canadian Corporate Residence and Statutory Recourse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Holding directors' and shareholders' meetings entirely outside Canada, failing to keep registered books and corporate records in Ontario, or failing to file annual corporate returns under the Ontario Business Corporations Act; CRA will often assert that the corporation is a 'treaty-shopping conduit' and can disregard its Canadian residence, or that it has ceased to exist in fact.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act, the corporation may be deemed non-resident, losing access to the 112(1) dividend deduction and becoming subject to a 25% withholding tax on every distribution made to its shareholders; Ontario corporate statute filings may be administratively dissolved or struck from the register after repeated default, ceasing the corporation's legal capacity to sue or defend and rendering all contracts unenforceable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a dissolved or non-resident-deemed corporation are personally liable for the corporation's debts incurred after dissolution without their knowledge; recovery under the Ontario Business Corporations Act section 248 for defective filings may subject directors to restitution of assets and statutory fines; in severe cases, personal travel bans and revocation of Canadian eTA or business visitor status may be ordered by the courts as a condition of dealing with the corporation's tax liabilities.
